html: Sri Lanka is famous for iconic waterfalls like Bambarakanda, Diyaluma, and Ravana Falls. However, beyond these popular attractions lies a hidden world of secret waterfalls, natural plunge pools, and untouched swimming spots waiting to be discovered. These off-the-beaten-path locations offer travelers peaceful surroundings, crystal-clear waters, and authentic nature experiences far from tourist crowds.

If you are an adventure traveler, nature lover, or photographer, exploring Sri Lanka’s hidden waterfalls and natural swimming holes is an unforgettable experience. This guide provides a traveler-friendly itinerary and insider tips to discover Sri Lanka’s best secret waterfalls safely and authentically.

text: Why Explore Hidden Waterfalls in Sri Lanka?

html: Sri Lanka’s central highlands and rainforest regions create the perfect environment for hundreds of waterfalls, many of which remain undiscovered by mass tourism. These hidden waterfalls offer:
Unlike popular tourist waterfalls, these secret locations allow you to experience Sri Lanka’s natural beauty in its purest form.
1. Secret Pools Near Bambarakanda Falls (Sri Lanka’s Tallest Waterfall)

Bambarakanda Falls, located in the Badulla District, is the tallest waterfall in Sri Lanka at 263 meters. While most visitors stop at the main viewpoint, few explore the side trails that lead to hidden plunge pools and natural swimming areas.
What Makes It Special:
The surrounding pine forest contains several small natural pools formed by mountain streams. These pools are clean, cool, and ideal for swimming.
How to Get There:
From Kalupahana village, take the Bambarakanda Falls road and follow local hiking trails through the forest. A short hike of 20–40 minutes leads to quieter, hidden swimming spots.
Best Time to Visit:
January to April and July to September offer the safest water levels and best swimming conditions.
2. Diyaluma Falls Upper Pools – Natural Infinity Pools
Diyaluma Falls is Sri Lanka’s second tallest waterfall, but its upper pools remain a hidden treasure. These natural infinity pools offer breathtaking views of the valley below.
Why Travelers Love It:

items: Natural rock pools perfect for swimming
Less crowded compared to the main waterfall

html: Hiking Details:
A moderate hike of about 45 minutes is required to reach the upper pools. The trail starts near Poonagala village.
Safety Tip:
Avoid visiting during heavy rains, as water flow can become dangerous.
3. Kirindi Ella Hidden Pools – Peaceful Jungle Escape
Kirindi Ella, located near Pelmadulla, is one of Sri Lanka’s lesser-known waterfalls. While the main waterfall is accessible, the upstream area features several secret natural swimming pools.
Highlights:

items: Calm, shallow pools suitable for swimming
Peaceful atmosphere with very few tourists

html: This location is perfect for travelers seeking relaxation and solitude.
4. Lanka Ella Secret Swimming Area – Near Ella Town
Most travelers visiting Ella miss Lanka Ella waterfall, which is less crowded compared to Ravana Falls. The area includes hidden natural pools ideal for swimming.
Why Visit Lanka Ella:

items: Quiet environment away from busy tourist spots

html: You can combine this visit with a scenic train journey and hiking experience.
5. Secret Waterfalls Near Belihuloya
Belihuloya is one of Sri Lanka’s best destinations for hidden waterfalls and natural swimming spots. The area is surrounded by mountains, forests, and rivers.
Hidden Gems in Belihuloya:

items: Small unnamed waterfalls along trekking trails

html: These locations offer perfect opportunities for swimming, hiking, and nature photography.
6. Upper Aberdeen Falls Natural Pools
Aberdeen Falls is located in the Nuwara Eliya District. While the base waterfall is popular, the upper stream contains hidden swimming spots.
Why It’s Unique:
The hike to the upper pools is suitable for moderate adventure travelers.
7. Galboda Ella Hidden Swimming Locations
Galboda Ella, located near Hatton, is a beautiful waterfall surrounded by lush forest. The upstream area features safe natural pools perfect for swimming.
Best Features:
This is an excellent destination for eco-tourism travelers.

These areas contain the highest concentration of waterfalls in Sri Lanka.
Best Time to Visit Hidden Waterfalls in Sri Lanka

The best months to explore hidden waterfalls are:

  • December to April

  • June to September

Avoid peak monsoon seasons, as water levels can become dangerous.
Safety Tips for Swimming in Natural Waterfalls
When visiting hidden waterfalls in Sri Lanka, always follow these safety guidelines:

items: Travel with a guide if possible
Respect local advice and warning signs

html: Safety should always be your top priority.
